Guards enumerated from `git diff -U0` (integration-test-revert-verify §A8). Recorded runs: see PR body. ⚠ M6 and M7 redden N8 / N3 too: N8 asserts the reported line NAMES the property and N3 asserts the line COUNT after addressing the conflicting name, so both follow from the mutant's semantics on those axes' own subject — the first recorded run showed the prediction was under-specified, not the axes over-broad (integration-test-revert-verify §A44). ⛤ Two guards of the diff carry no mutant of their own and are TRANSITIVELY covered, named here so the next reader does not read them as a hole: the early `if (message === undefined) return;` in report() (a name with no recorded conflict) is exercised by every silent axis — N1 N3 N4 N7 N8 N9 all address names that have no conflict and must stay quiet, and M3 shows the branch is load-bearing by reddening exactly those; and the `this.report(conflicts, name)` call inside declaredRange() is exercised by N2 N5 N9 (M7, which empties the warn call it leads to, reddens them). ⛤ Round 2 (2026-09-20): the axis set gained N10/N11 (an INJECTED property counts as written), and the measured red sets grew by N10 under M3 M4 M6 M7 — each follows from that mutant's semantics on N10's own subject (it addresses a conflicting name and asserts both the line count and that the line NAMES ems__Effort_status), so the lists record the measurement.
